newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials firm.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials firmed early Friday, pushing prices higher against a modest drop in the underlying NYMEX futures contract, traders said.
Agricultural demand and delays on the Houston-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline system that pushed liftings back by five days and will persist through May were cited as factors in early talk.
Gasoline differentials were steady in morning trade in the Chicago and Group Three markets as traders wound down a relatively lackluster week of trade in the spot markets.
"The Explorer delays seem to be having some effect," one trader said of the jump in Group Three diesel differentials.
Low sulphur diesel was bid 7.0 cents a gallon over NYMEX May heating oil in Group Three and 2.50 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
High sulphur also firmed to 6.50/6.75 cents over the print in Group Three and 1.50/2.0 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
The firming differentials offset a nearly 0.25 cent a gallon drop in the underlying front-month heating oil contract, while NYMEX May unleaded was off nearly 0.50 cent a gallon in late-morning trade.
Unleaded gasoline differentials were unchanged at 0.25 cent a gallon under to even with NYMEX May unleaded in Chicago and 0.50/0.25 cent under the print in Group Three, traders said.
